The more she rehearsed scenarios in her head, the more she felt trapped by the idea that she was fundamentally incapable of handling her own life, reinforcing her negative self-image. Each time the memory surfaced, she found herself convinced that she was a target, not just a victim of circumstance, but someone marked by her past, leading her to feel unsafe in even the most mundane situations. Each recollection would intensify her fears, causing her to feel unsafe unless she could position herself with her back against a wall, a desperate attempt to regain some sense of control over her environment.
